"In January 1977, after nineteen months of authoritarian Emergency rule, Prime Minister Indira Gandhi unexpectedly announced that elections to the Lok Sabha would be held in March. Faced with calls for her resignation, on the night of 25 June 1975, Indira Gandhi advised President Fakhruddin Ali Ahmed to proclaim a National Emergency under Article 352 on the subjective grounds of 'internal disturbance'. NCERT Class 12 Contemporary World Politics (Chapter 9: Globalisation, pp. 136-141): Globalisation impacts are divided into three clear categories: (1) Political (erosion of state capacity), (2) Economic (trade deregulation, FDI flows, WTO rules, deregulation of industries), and (3) Cultural (threat to indigenous cultures, western cultural homogenisation, burger/blue jeans culture, cultural exchange, and heterogenisation).
